_note: Care is the nurse's day: offers matched by scope, distance, continuity and Trust Score, the visit started and completed with the visit code, the protocol checklist, capture, handover, offline sync, and the lists a nurse works from. Wave 2 contract; Wave 3 build.

refusals.statement: Nobody without a current Trust Score is offered a visit.
refusals.why: No score, no dispatch: the rule Verify enforces at the bus.

refusals.statement: A visit starts and completes only with the visit code.
refusals.why: The code is the proof the right nurse is at the right door.

refusals.statement: A nurse's location is not shared beyond the visit.
refusals.why: Tracking is on the day, for the visit, and ends with it.

refusals.statement: A supervised carer is not dispatched without their registered nurse.
refusals.why: Supervision ratios are enforced in dispatch or not at all.

refusals.statement: This visit is set to wait for the record to confirm its encounter is signed, and no record route answers Care yet: GET /fhir/{resourceType}/{id} does not take calls from the Care engine. It is not handed over or completed until one does.
refusals.why: The setting encounter-entry-counts-as-signed in packages/catalog/care.json is switched off for this visit. It is an engine refusal rather than one on the handover and completion routes, because both frozen routes answer it and neither route's shape changes. Its answeredBy names both, and the runtime refuses it from any other route, so it is frozen with them in packages/catalog/apis.refusals.lock rather than beside them.

refusals.statement: This visit is set to wait for the record to confirm its encounter is signed, and the record route that would say so, GET /v1/record/encounter-statuses/{encounterRef}, is proposed and not built. It is not handed over or completed until that route answers Care.
refusals.why: The setting encounter-entry-counts-as-signed in packages/catalog/care.json is switched off for this visit. encounter-signature-unconfirmed said no record route took calls from Care; since 15 September one is declared for Care in packages/catalog/apis/record.json, and naming it is new words, so it is a new id rather than an edit to a frozen one. Its answeredBy names version two of the handover and completion routes, which were versioned to answer it.

routes.summary: Offer a visit to the best eligible clinician.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The visit to fill.
The service, which sets the scope needed.

response.why: When it lapses to the next clinician.

refusals.statement: Nobody without a current Trust Score is offered a visit.
refusals.why: Verify ranks; Care never offers past a failed gate.

refusals.statement: A supervised carer is not offered a visit without their registered nurse.
refusals.why: Supervision is enforced in the offer.

refusals.statement: That service is not offered yet, so nobody is matched to it.
refusals.why: A service later than the seed phase in packages/catalog/care.json has nobody who has agreed to deliver it.

refusals.statement: Everybody eligible for this visit has been asked, so it goes to a dispatcher.
refusals.why: An offer is never made to somebody a gate withheld just to fill the visit.

refusals.statement: Nobody is offered a visit until Care knows the suburb it is in.
refusals.why: booking.requested carries no zone, and a distance measured to nowhere would rank nobody honestly.

withdrawn.why: It had no refusal for a visit the patient asked to wait for a named nurse, so when she could not be offered it the only true answers left were to send somebody the patient did not ask for or to say everybody eligible had been asked, which was false. And its visit-zone-unknown reasoning still said booking.requested carries no zone, which version two of that event corrected. Version two adds waiting-for-named-nurse and keeps the row that says the patient was told. Its callers are version two's.

routes.summary: Offer a visit to the best eligible clinician, or, where the patient asked to wait for a nurse by name, to her alone.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The visit to fill.
The service, which sets the scope needed.

response.why: When it lapses: to the next clinician, or, for a visit waiting for a named nurse, back to her while the visit's hour has not come.

refusals.statement: Nobody without a current Trust Score is offered a visit.
refusals.why: Verify ranks; Care never offers past a failed gate.

refusals.statement: A supervised carer is not offered a visit without their registered nurse.
refusals.why: Supervision is enforced in the offer.

refusals.statement: That service is not offered yet, so nobody is matched to it.
refusals.why: A service later than the seed phase in packages/catalog/care.json has nobody who has agreed to deliver it.

refusals.statement: Everybody eligible for this visit has been asked, so it goes to a dispatcher.
refusals.why: An offer is never made to somebody a gate withheld just to fill the visit.

refusals.statement: Nobody is offered a visit until Care knows the suburb it is in.
refusals.why: booking.requested@2 carries the zone id, and Care refuses one packages/catalog/geography.json does not hold: a distance measured to a suburb the map has no centre for would rank nobody honestly.

refusals.statement: This visit is waiting for the nurse the patient asked for by name, and she cannot be offered it now, so nobody else is asked. It goes to a dispatcher, and the patient is told.
refusals.why: The patient answered wait, from packages/catalog/booking.json person.fallback. Care re-offers her the visit each time an offer to her lapses, while its hour has not come; she cannot be offered it when a gate withholds her, when she declined it, or when the hour came before she took it. Giving it to the next nurse then would send somebody the patient did not ask for, which is the one thing their answer refused.

keptOnRefusal.why: A refused offer is rolled back, and the one thing a refusal for a waiting visit must keep is the row saying the patient is to be told she cannot take it, with the answer and the settings version it was decided under. Without it the visit waits and nobody is told. It is one row about one visit, never an offer and never a booking.

routes.summary: Accept an offer.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The offer.

refusals.statement: That offer has lapsed.
refusals.why: It went to the next clinician.

refusals.statement: That offer was made to somebody else.
refusals.why: An offer is personal.

routes.summary: Decline an offer.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same act once.
The offer.

refusals.statement: That offer has already lapsed.
refusals.why: Nothing to decline.

refusals.statement: That offer was made to somebody else.
refusals.why: An offer is personal, and so is turning it down.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: Declining ends one offer; the next is made through POST /v1/care/offers, which emits it.

routes.summary: Start a visit with the visit code.

request.why: The visit.
The code the patient gives at the door.

refusals.statement: The visit code did not match, so the visit has not started.
refusals.why: A failed code stops the visit.

refusals.statement: That visit is not today.
refusals.why: A visit starts on its day.

routes.summary: Record the protocol checklist for the visit.

request.why: The visit.
The ratified protocol, id@version.
Checklist item ids completed.

refusals.statement: A checklist runs only under a ratified protocol.
refusals.why: An unratified checklist is a list of guesses in a clinical record.

refusals.statement: No checklist is recorded against a visit that has not started.
refusals.why: A checklist is a record of a visit that is happening.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: The checklist is part of the encounter, written through the gateway.

routes.summary: Attach observations already written through the gateway to the visit.

request.why: The visit.
Observation entries in the Passport.

refusals.statement: Nothing is captured against a visit that has not started.
refusals.why: Readings belong to a visit that happened.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: The observations were written through the gateway, which emitted passport.entry.written.

request.why: The visit.
The encounter to review.

response.why: Whether it went into the clinical inbox.

refusals.statement: The encounter has required sections missing.
refusals.why: A doctor reviews a complete encounter, not a draft.

refusals.statement: A visit that has not started is not handed to a doctor.
refusals.why: A doctor reviews what a nurse found at a visit that happened.

Its shape is unchanged. Its callers are version two's.

routes.summary: Hand the visit to a doctor for review, refused in the record route's own name while the encounter's signature cannot be confirmed.

request.why: The visit.
The encounter to review.

response.why: Whether it went into the clinical inbox.

refusals.why: A doctor reviews a complete encounter, not a draft.

refusals.statement: A visit that has not started is not handed to a doctor.
refusals.why: A doctor reviews what a nurse found at a visit that happened.

request.why: The visit.
The patient's code again, at the end.
The signed encounter.

refusals.statement: The visit code did not match, so the visit is not complete.
refusals.why: Completion is confirmed by the patient, not assumed.

refusals.statement: The encounter is not signed.
refusals.why: A visit is complete when its record is.

refusals.statement: A visit that never started cannot be completed.
refusals.why: Completion confirms a visit the code opened; without a start there is nothing to confirm.

withdrawn.why: The engine refusal it answered, encounter-signature-unconfirmed, says no record route takes calls from Care. request.why: The visit.
The patient's code again, at the end.
The signed encounter.

refusals.statement: The visit code did not match, so the visit is not complete.
refusals.why: Completion is confirmed by the patient, not assumed.

refusals.statement: The encounter is not signed.
refusals.why: A visit is complete when its record is.

refusals.statement: A visit that never started cannot be completed.
refusals.why: Completion confirms a visit the code opened; without a start there is nothing to confirm.

routes.summary: Upload the offline queue.

request.why: The batch, chosen on the phone.
The queued operations, in order.

response.why: Operations shown back to the nurse.

refusals.statement: A conflict is shown to the nurse, never merged silently.
refusals.why: Two versions of a visit merged by software is a record nobody wrote.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A sync replays calls that each emit their own events.

withdrawn.why: It sent operation references and nothing else, and packages/catalog/capture.json's conflicts cannot be decided without each operation's visit, its observation and the time the phone took it: a duplicate is the same measure twice in one visit, a stale write is a reading for a visit already completed, and clock skew is the phone's time against the server's. It was never built. Its callers are version two's.

routes.summary: Upload the offline queue of readings captured with no signal, each with its visit, its observation and the time the phone took it, and be shown every conflict rather than have one merged.

request.why: Chosen by the phone for this upload. The same key twice is the same batch once, answered again rather than applied again.

The batch, as the phone names it in the queue it shows the nurse. A batch this nurse already sent is answered with its first answer whatever key a retry carries, and another nurse's batch of the same name is her own.
The queued operations, in the order the nurse took them.

fields.why: The operation, as the phone queued it. A conflict or a refusal is shown back by it.
What was queued, one of packages/catalog/care.json sync.operationKinds. Only a capture travels this way.
The visit the reading belongs to, named as every Care visit route names it. A reading for a visit already completed is a stale write.
The observation entry the Passport gateway already wrote. The reading travels there and never here.
Which measure in packages/catalog/records.json observations.measures the entry is of, and never its value. The same measure twice in one visit is a duplicate a clinician decides.
When the phone believed it took the reading. Kept beside the server's receipt time and never presented as when it happened; ahead of the server is clock skew.

response.why: Every reading attached, in server order.

fields.why: The operation attached.
The server's receipt time, which orders it.
What the phone believed, kept beside it.
Whether the phone's time was ahead of the server's, which the server resolves by ordering on its own.

response.why: Every operation shown back to the nurse and not applied.

fields.why: The operation not applied.
The conflict's id in packages/catalog/capture.json conflicts, whose name and detail a screen shows.

response.why: Operations the visit would not take at all, each with the refusal a direct capture would have answered.

fields.why: The operation refused.
The refusal POST /v1/care/visits/{appointmentRef}/capture@1 or the shared list declares, whose sentence a screen shows.

response.why: This route's conflict-not-merged sentence, present whenever a conflict is shown, so the nurse reads why nothing was merged in the contract's words.

refusals.statement: A conflict is shown to the nurse, never merged silently.
refusals.why: Two versions of a visit merged by software is a record nobody wrote. The batch is answered rather than refused when some operations conflict, because refusing would roll back the readings that did not; the sentence travels in notMerged.

refusals.statement: An operation in this batch does not name its visit, its observation entry, the measure it is of and the time the phone took it, so nothing in the batch was applied.
refusals.why: Every conflict rule needs all four. An operation without them could only be applied by guessing which rule it escaped, and a batch half-applied round a malformed operation is a queue nobody can reason about.

refusals.statement: Only a reading captured with no signal is replayed from a queue. A start, a handover or a completion is not, so nothing in the batch was applied.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/care.json sync.whyOnlyCapture: each of the others asks something of somebody at the moment it happens, and replaying one an hour later answers that question on the patient's behalf.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A reading was written through the Passport gateway, which emitted passport.entry.written; attaching it to the visit is Care's own bookkeeping, as POST /v1/care/visits/{appointmentRef}/capture@1 is.

routes.summary: Read your shifts.

refusals.statement: Those shifts are somebody else's.
refusals.why: A roster shows a nurse her own day.

routes.summary: Read the services offered where you are.

request.why: Where the visit would be.

refusals.statement: MyThuso does not visit there yet.
refusals.why: Better to say so than list services nobody can deliver.

routes.summary: Read open locum shifts at hospitals and care homes.

refusals.statement: Locum shifts are shown only to verified locums.
refusals.why: A shift is an offer of work.

routes.summary: Read the rural circuit routes.

refusals.statement: That circuit is not running yet.
refusals.why: An unpublished route is not a promise.

routes.summary: Read Care's settings in force — how long an offer lasts, who may be offered the visits no named scope covers, and whether an Encounter entry counts as signed — each with its default and who decided it, what an admin may set, its clinical review, and every change made to them.

response.why: The version in force. A change is made against it, and whatever starts now keeps it.

Each setting: its key, type, unit, the value in force and the version that set it, its default and provenance, its limits, who may change it, what a change reaches, its guardrail, and its clinical review.

fields.why: The setting's key, which a change names.
Its name on the Configuration screen.
The question it answers, as a sentence.
One of the types in packages/catalog/settings.json.
What the value is counted in, or null for a type that has none.
The value in force: a number, a switch, a word, a list, a rota or a record, as its type gives.
The settings version that set the value in force, 1 for the contract's default.
The contract's default, of the same kind as the value in force.
Who decided the default, when and why, or who proposed it and why, and who reviewed it where somebody did.
What an admin may set — the bounds, allowed values, roles, posts, items or parts its type carries — with their provenance.
The roles that may change it, resolved from the contract and the settings in force.
What a change reaches, as a sentence.
The sentence no value may break, or null for a setting with none.
The capability whose holder confirms its clinical review, or null for a setting that waits on nobody.
Who confirmed the clinical review of the value in force, or null while it is not clinically reviewed.
The reviewer's reference.
When the review was confirmed through the review route, or null for a default reviewed before it shipped.
The day a default was reviewed before it shipped, or null for a review confirmed through the route.

response.why: Every accepted change, oldest first: which setting, from, to, who, when and why. Nothing in it is edited or removed.

fields.why: The version this change made.
The setting it changed.
The value before, of the kind its type gives.
The value after.
Why, as it was written.
The role of the person who made it.
The reference of the person who made it, from the caller the runtime admitted.
When it was made.

refusals.statement: Only somebody who may change these settings reads them and who changed them.
refusals.why: The history names the people who changed how an engine behaves. It is read by the roles that may change it.

withdrawn.why: Withdrawn by the Clinical Safety lead in Wave 5. It admitted an admin and a doctor, the doctor from the vetting register's grant of sign-clinical-review, so a nurse Clinical's review-confirmer setting names could not read the value she is asked to confirm. Version two admits every role that setting may name, and the handler reads who confirms from Clinical in force.

routes.summary: Change one Care setting, with a reason, against the version in force. It applies to offers made after it and never to one already made.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same change once, and the history gains one row.
The setting's key, from the settings block of the engine's own contract.
The new value, for a setting in minutes, a count, cents or a percentage.
The new value, for a setting that is on or off.
The new value, for a setting that is one of a few named choices.
The new wording, for a setting patients or nurses read.
The new roles, for a setting that names roles from packages/catalog/vetting.json.
The new rota, for a setting that is windows of a post, days and hours. A post, never a named person.

fields.why: The post the window is for, by its id in the setting's posts. Never a named person.
The days of the week it covers, from the days packages/catalog/settings.json lists.
When it opens, as hours and minutes from 00:00.
When it closes, after it opens and no later than 24:00.

request.why: The new values, for a setting that is a list.
The new values, for a setting whose parts change together.
Why. Asked for by the handler rather than the binder, so that a change without one is refused in its own sentence rather than the general one for a missing field.
The settings version the admin was looking at. A change against an older one is refused.

response.why: When it took effect. Whatever started before it keeps the version it started under.

refusals.statement: Only the role a setting names changes it, and the change is recorded against a named person.
refusals.why: A setting decides how the platform treats people. The role or capability the setting names changes it, and a change is recorded against somebody who can be asked about it; everybody else only reads what is in force.

refusals.statement: There is no setting by that name.
refusals.why: An unknown setting is refused rather than stored, or the history fills with changes nothing reads.

refusals.statement: A change to a setting says why, or it is not made.
refusals.why: The history is read after something has gone wrong. A change with no reason is a number somebody moved.

refusals.statement: These settings changed after you opened them. Read what is in force now and decide against that.
refusals.why: Two admins changing one setting from screens opened at the same time would each overwrite a decision they never saw.

refusals.statement: That is not the kind of value this setting holds.
refusals.why: A word where a number belongs, or a list where one choice belongs, is a guess at what the admin meant, and a setting is never set by a guess.

refusals.statement: This setting is never nought or less, whatever its range says.
refusals.why: A wait of nothing, an offer that lapses as it is made and a fee of nothing are never what anybody meant. The range is a proposal and could be set wrongly; this refusal does not depend on it.

refusals.statement: Every role a setting names is a role on the vetting register.
refusals.why: A role the register does not hold is a gate nobody can be vetted through, which looks like a shortage rather than a mistake.

refusals.statement: That wording is longer than this setting allows.
refusals.why: The maximum is the space the words are read in. Wording that does not fit is cut off where somebody reads it.

refusals.statement: That wording drops a sentence this setting must always keep.
refusals.why: Some wording carries a promise that protects somebody. It may be reworded around that sentence and never without it.

refusals.statement: That rota leaves hours uncovered that must always have somebody on them.
refusals.why: A rota with a gap is an alert with nobody to go to, and nobody finds out until one arrives.

refusals.statement: That is outside what an admin may set for this setting.
refusals.why: The bounds, the allowed values and the allowed roles sit beside the default in the engine's contract. Moving a setting past them is a change to that contract, not a setting.

refusals.statement: That is already the value in force, so there is nothing to change.
refusals.why: A change that changes nothing is a row in the history saying something happened when nothing did.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: No engine acts on a settings change. The engine that owns a setting reads the value in force when it starts something, and the event contract refuses an event nobody subscribes to. A change is the row it appends to the engine's own history, which the read route returns.

routes.summary: Confirm the clinical review of the value in force for a Care setting that waits on one: who may be offered an injection, a family planning or a sick-note visit, and whether an Encounter entry counts as signed. A doctor holds sign-clinical-review.

request.why: Chosen by the caller. The same key twice is the same confirmation once.
The setting's key, from the settings block of the engine's own contract.

The version that set the value being confirmed: 1 for the contract's default, or the version of the change. A reviewer confirms a value they read, never whatever happens to be in force when the request lands.
Why the value is clinically safe. Asked for by the handler, so a confirmation without one is refused in its own sentence.

refusals.statement: Only somebody holding the capability this setting names confirms its clinical review, and the confirmation is recorded against a named person.
refusals.why: A clinical-scope setting decides who may do what to a patient. Confirming it is a clinician's act, attributed like a signed review.

refusals.statement: There is no setting by that name.
refusals.why: An unknown setting is refused rather than stored, or the reviews fill with confirmations of nothing.

refusals.statement: This setting does not wait on a clinical review.
refusals.why: A confirmation of a setting nobody asked a clinician about reads, later, as if one had been needed.

refusals.statement: A clinical review says why the value is safe, or it is not recorded.
refusals.why: A confirmation with no reason is a signature under nothing.

refusals.statement: That is not the value in force for this setting. Review what is in force now.
refusals.why: A reviewer confirms the value they read. A value replaced since is not the one patients are being treated under.

refusals.statement: That value has already been clinically reviewed.
refusals.why: Two confirmations of one value are one review recorded twice.

refusals.statement: Nobody confirms the clinical review of a change they made themselves.
refusals.why: packages/catalog/vetting.json's selfActionRefusals, applied to settings: a review by the person who made the change is no review.

routes.emitsNoneBecause: A confirmation changes no value, so nothing acts differently because of it. It is the row it appends to the engine's own reviews, which the read route returns.

withdrawn.why: Withdrawn by the Clinical Safety lead in Wave 5. It admitted a doctor alone, from the vetting register's grant of sign-clinical-review, so who confirms a clinical review of Care's scope was decided by the register rather than by Clinical's review-confirmer setting, which an admin changes. Version two admits every clinical role that setting may name, and confirms only for the roles it names in force.
